readings.title: Strife, Wisdom, and Folly
readings.subtitle: Better is a dry morsel with peace than a house full of feasting with strife.
readings.text: [Proverbs 17:1] Better is a dry piece of bread and rest with it, Than a house filled with slaughters of strife. [2] A wise servant rules over a son who causes shame, And shares an inheritance among the brothers. [3] A refining pot is for silver and a furnace for gold, But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> tries <dn>את</dn> the hearts. [4] An evil-doer gives heed to wicked lips; A liar gives ear to a tongue of desire. [5] <dn>He</dn> who mocks the poor reproaches <dn>את</dn> <dn>his</dn> Maker; <dn>He</dn> who rejoices at calamity does not go unpunished. [6] Children’s children are the crown of old men, And the adornment of children is their fathers. [7] Excellent speech is not fitting for a fool, Much less lying lips for a noble. [8] A bribe is a stone of favour in the eyes of its owner; Wherever <dn>he</dn> turns, <dn>he</dn> prospers. [9] <dn>He</dn> who covers <dn>את</dn> a transgression seeks love, But <dn>he</dn> who repeats a matter separates intimate friends. [10] Reproof enters deeper into a wise man Than a hundred strikes on a fool. [11] An evil one seeks only rebellion, So a cruel messenger is sent against him. [12] Let a bereaved bear meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly. [13] Whoever rewards evil for good, Evil does not leave <dn>את</dn> his house. [14] The beginning of strife is like releasing water; Therefore stop fighting before it breaks out.

readings.title: Justice, Friendship, and a Joyful Heart
readings.subtitle: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
readings.text: [Proverbs 17:15] <dn>He</dn> who declares the wrong right, And <dn>he</dn> who condemns <dn>את</dn> the righteous, Both of them are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] Why is this – a price in the hand Of a fool to buy wisdom, When there is no heart? [17] A friend loves at all times, And a brother is born for adversity. [18] A man lacking heart shakes hands in a pledge, <dn>He</dn> becomes a guarantor for his friend. [19] <dn>He</dn> who loves transgression loves strife, <dn>He</dn> who exalts his door seeks destruction. [20] <dn>He</dn> who has a crooked heart finds no good, And <dn>he</dn> who has a perverse tongue falls into evil. [21] <dn>He</dn> who brings forth <dn>את</dn> a fool has sorrow for it, And the father of a fool has no joy. [22] A rejoicing heart causes good healing, But a stricken spirit dries the bones. [23] One who is wrong accepts a bribe behind the back To pervert the paths of right-ruling. [24] Wisdom is before the face of the understanding one, But the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth. [25] A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her who bore him. [26] It is also not good to punish the righteous one, To strike noble ones for straightness. [27] <dn>He</dn> who has knowledge spares his words, And a man of understanding is cool of spirit. [28] Even a fool keeping silence is regarded as wise, As understanding, when <dn>he</dn> closes his lips.

readings.title: Integrity, Wealth, and Divine Justice
readings.subtitle: Better is the poor walking in his integrity than one of perverse lips, who is a fool.
readings.text: [Proverbs 19:1] Better is the poor walking in his integrity Than one of perverse lips, who is a fool. [2] Also, desire without knowledge is not good; And <dn>he</dn> who hurries with his feet sins. [3] The foolishness of a man perverts <dn>את</dn> his way, And his heart is wroth against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] Wealth adds many friends, But the poor is separated from his friend. [5] A false witness does not go unpunished, And <dn>he</dn> who breaths out lies does not escape. [6] Many entreat the favour of the noble. And all are friends to him who gives gifts. [7] All the brothers of the poor shall hate him; How much more shall his friends go far from him! <dn>He</dn> pursues promises – they are gone!. [8] <dn>He</dn> who gets heart loves <dn>את</dn> his own life; <dn>He</dn> who guards understanding finds good. [9] A false witness does not go unpunished, And <dn>he</dn> who breathes out lies perishes. [10] Luxury is not fitting for a fool, Much less for a servant to rule over princes. [11] A man’s discretion makes him patient, And his adorning is to pass over a transgression. [12] The sovereign’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, But his delight is like dew on the grass.

readings.title: Family, Diligence, and the Counsel of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Many are the plans in a man’s heart, but it is the counsel of YeHoVaH that stands.
readings.text: [Proverbs 19:13] A foolish son is a calamity to his father, And the contentions of a wife are a continual dripping. [14] Houses and riches are the inheritance from fathers, But an understanding wife is from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] Laziness makes one fall into a deep sleep, And an idle being suffers hunger. [16] <dn>He</dn> who guards <dn>את</dn> the command guards <dn>את</dn> his life, <dn>He</dn> who despises <dn>His</dn> ways dies. [17] <dn>He</dn> who shows favour to the poor lends to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And <dn>He</dn> repays <dn>את</dn> his deed. [18] Discipline <dn>את</dn> your son because there is expectation, And do not set <dn>את</dn> your being on his destruction. [19] One of great wrath bears punishment; For if you rescue him, You only have to do it again. [20] Listen to counsel and accept <dn>את</dn> discipline, So that you are wise in your latter end. [21] Many are the plans in a man’s heart, But it is the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that stands.

readings.title: Character, Discipline, and Judgment
readings.subtitle: The fear of YeHoVaH leads to life, and he remains satisfied.
readings.text: [Proverbs 19:22] What is desirable in a man is his loving-commitment, And a poor man is better than a liar. [23] The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> leads to life, And <dn>he</dn> remains satisfied, <dn>He</dn> is not visited by evil. [24] A lazy one buries his hand in a dish, And does not bring it back to his mouth. [25] Strike <dn>את</dn> a scoffer, and the simple is made wise; And reprove one who has understanding, And <dn>he</dn> discerns knowledge. [26] <dn>He</dn> who plunders <dn>את</dn> a father, Chases away <dn>את</dn> his mother, Is a son causing shame and bringing reproach. [27] Cease, my son, to hear discipline, And you shall stray from the words of knowledge. [28] A witness of Beliya‛al scorns right-ruling, And the mouth of the wrong ones Devours <dn>את</dn> wickedness. [29] Judgments are in store for scoffers, And beatings for the backs of fools.
